issue_context.title: Replication with multiple servers using different SSL options.
issue_context.body:
<!--

## Issue Description
I've set up multiple instances of MySQL in google cloud.  Each instance has its own unique CERT, KEY, and CA.    

When I look at the code that sets up connection options  (MysqlDriver.prototype.createConnectionOptions) 
It has: 
```typescript
    MysqlDriver.prototype.createConnectionOptions = function (options, credentials) {
        credentials = Object.assign({}, credentials, DriverUtils_1.DriverUtils.buildDriverOptions(credentials)); // todo: do it better way
        // build connection options for the driver
        var obj =  Object.assign({}, {
            charset: options.charset,
            timezone: options.timezone,
            connectTimeout: options.connectTimeout,
            insecureAuth: options.insecureAuth,
            supportBigNumbers: options.supportBigNumbers !== undefined ? options.supportBigNumbers : true,
            bigNumberStrings: options.bigNumberStrings !== undefined ? options.bigNumberStrings : true,
            dateStrings: options.dateStrings,
            debug: options.debug,
            trace: options.trace,
            multipleStatements: options.multipleStatements,
            flags: options.flags
        }, {
            host: credentials.host,
            user: credentials.username,
            password: credentials.password,
            database: credentials.database,
            port: credentials.port,
            ssl: options.ssl,
            socketPath: credentials.socketPath
        }, options.acquireTimeout === undefined
            ? {}
            : { acquireTimeout: options.acquireTimeout }, options.extra || {});
        
            return obj;
    };
```

It looks like its always pulling the parent options for SSL.  When in fact we need the SSL options as defined on the credentials as each server has its own keys. 

Here is the configuration we are using: 
When I set up Type ORM, I  done this:

```typescript
  createConnection({
    type: "mysql",
    entities: [__dirname + "/entity/**/*.ts"],
    synchronize: true,
    logging: true,
    replication: {
      master: {
        port: 3306,
          host: "XX.XX.XX.XX",
          database:  "DB"
          username: "USER", 
          password: "MY PW2"
          ssl: {
            ca: "CA TEXT"
            key: "KEY TEXT"
            cert: "CERT TEXT"
          },
      },
      slaves: [
        {
          port: 3306,
          host: "XX.XX.XX.XX",
          database:  "DB"
          username: "USER", 
          password: "MY PW2"
          ssl: {
            ca: "CA TEXT"
            key: "KEY TEXT"
            cert: "CERT TEXT"
          },
        },
      ],
    },
  })
```
When I run, I keep getting failed, user not authorized. And this is a result of the KEY's not matching. as its always only pulling the parent SSL option from the root. 

### Expected Behavior
We would expect it to use the ca options for each credential specified.  If no keys are specified, it could continue to do what it does today and fall back to the root.  
(IE: ssl: credentials.ssl != undefined ? credentials.ssl : options.ssl ) 


### Actual Behavior
Its always selecting the root options and we are not able to query. 


### Steps to Reproduce

1. set up a connection with different servers that each use its own CA configurations. 
```typescript
 createConnection({
    type: "mysql",
    entities: [__dirname + "/entity/**/*.ts"],
    synchronize: true,
    logging: true,
    replication: {
      master: {
        port: 3306,
          host: "XX.XX.XX.XX",
          database:  "DB"
          username: "USER", 
          password: "MY PW2"
          ssl: {
            ca: "CA TEXT"
            key: "KEY TEXT"
            cert: "CERT TEXT"
          },
      },
      slaves: [
        {
          port: 3306,
          host: "XX.XX.XX.XX",
          database:  "DB"
          username: "USER", 
          password: "MY PW2"
          ssl: {
            ca: "CA TEXT"
            key: "KEY TEXT"
            cert: "CERT TEXT"
          },
        },
      ],
    },
  })
```
2. Create A Connection
3. Run a simple query on each connection:
    
Observe the issue

```typescript
  const masterQueryRunner = connection.createQueryRunner("master");
      try {
        const userFromMaster = await masterQueryRunner.query("SELECT * FROM user ", [], true);
      } finally {
        await masterQueryRunner.release();
      }

      const slaveQueryRunner = connection.createQueryRunner("slave");
      try {
        const userFromSlave = await slaveQueryRunner.query("SELECT * FROM user ", [], true);
      } finally {
        return slaveQueryRunner.release();
      }

```
